title: Courier
description: A road-worn courier, NCR-adjacent. Carries a battered satchel. Talks fast, trusts nobody.
backstory: The wasteland's most reliable courier doesn't remember much before the road — a deliberate choice, they'll tell you, after a job went wrong in a way they don't discuss. What they kept is this: every trade route from here to the Colorado, every settlement's preferred currency, and the name of every kid who's traded them scrap for a delivered message. Pip has seen the best and worst the wasteland can produce. They keep running anyway.

intro.video_speech: Name's Pip. Wasteland courier. I've walked four days to find you. Got a priority message from Vault-Tec.
intro.text:
Hey. You.

Don't reach for anything. I'm not hostile — just careful. Name's Pip. Wasteland courier. Been walking four days to find you.

Got a sealed message here from Vault-Tec Operations. They said — and I'm quoting — 'Deliver to the wanderer in the jumpsuit. Priority one.'

That's you, right? Tell me that's you.

responses.text: [Question] Who sent you? How'd you find me?
[Friendly] Yeah, that's me. Good to see a friendly face.
[Sarcastic] Priority one. Right. Let me guess — I owe someone caps.

node_who_sent.text:
Vault-Tec Operations — or what's left of 'em. They've got relay stations scattered across the Mojave, still broadcasting.

How'd I find you? Signal Runner beacon, triangulated your position. Scary accurate for two-hundred-year-old tech.

Look, I don't ask questions about my clients. I just deliver. You want the message or not?

node_friendly_response.text:
*snorts* Friendly. Sure. You haven't seen what I walked through to get here.

Still — you seem steady. Most people wake up out here half-mad from dehydration.

Here. The message. Read it. Then we can talk.

node_sarcastic_response.text:
*laughs, short and dry*

Not caps. Worse. They want your attention.

Vault-Tec Operations — the ghost of it, anyway — thinks you matter. I've delivered enough of these 'priority one' letters to know that either means you're very important... or very expendable.

Sometimes both.

responses.text: [Sarcastic] Sounds like every job I've ever had.

node_give_message.text:
*hands you a sealed envelope, cracked wax seal still intact*

— VAULT-TEC OPERATIONS MEMO —
To: Field Asset (You)
Re: Immediate Orientation Protocol

You've been issued standard Vault-Tec field gear. Your first task: get oriented. Check your inventory. Equip your sidearm. Tune your radio to the Atomic Fizz frequency. Then pull up your map.

The wasteland doesn't wait for you to be ready.
— VT Operations

*Pip crosses their arms*
"So. You taking the job?"

responses.text: [Accept] Yeah. I'm in. What do I need to know?
[Question] What's Atomic Fizz? What's the radio for?
[Sarcastic] 'Field asset.' I have a name, you know.
[Direct] I'm already moving. Thanks for the delivery.

grant_items.name: Vault 77 Security Sidearm
grant_items.description: Standard-issue sidearm carried by Vault 77 security personnel.

node_about_radio.text:
Atomic Fizz Radio. DJ Struggle runs it — broadcasts out of a fortified bunker somewhere in the Mojave.

Mixes music, news, wasteland intel. Warns about raider movements, radiation spikes, where to find clean water.

It's the closest thing to a news network out here. You want to survive? You listen to that radio.

The frequency's pre-loaded into your Pocket-Boy. Tune it.

node_have_a_name.text:
*raises an eyebrow*

"Yeah? What is it?"

...

*waits*

Look, I deliver to dozens of people. Half of 'em don't make it a week. I stop learning names. It's — it's a self-preservation thing.

But if you're the type to push back on Vault-Tec Operations paperwork... maybe you'll be in the other half.

Take the job. Prove me wrong.

node_accept_tips.text:
Good. Then listen up — I'm only saying this once.

Your inventory — check it. They packed you stimpaks, water, bobby pins, ammo. Don't lose the pins. You'd be amazed how many doors in this wasteland are still locked.

Sidearm — keep it on you. The safety's on. Take it off before you need it, not after.

The map — use it. Locations light up as you get close. Stick to the marked roads until you know the terrain.

And the radio... just keep it on. Some nights, it's the only friendly voice you'll hear.

responses.text: [Question] What can you tell me about this area?
[Question] Are you going to stick around?
[Direct] Got it. I'll figure the rest out.

node_accept_direct.text:
*nods once*

Good. That's the right attitude.

Inventory, sidearm, radio, map. In that order. Don't skip steps — the wasteland punishes overconfidence.

I'll be nearby for a while. You need anything, find me.

node_about_area.text:
This stretch? Mojave fringe. Used to be ranch land before the bombs.

Now it's... contested. Raiders work the northern highway. NCR remnants hold the south. In between is nobody's land — which is where you're standing.

Faction Zones light up on your map as you explore. Don't stumble into raider territory without a plan.

The Atomic Fizz locations — the ones marked with the bottle cap icon — those are usually safe to approach. Usually.

node_about_vault77.text:
*pauses, shifts weight*

Vault 77. People talk about it. Nobody goes near it.

Officially? Closed for decommissioning decades ago. Unofficially? The signals still broadcast. Automated systems, maybe. Or something else.

I've had three clients hired specifically to find it. None of them came back.

I'm not saying don't go. I'm saying... go prepared.

That's all I know.

node_stick_around.text:
*slight pause, then a half-shrug*

For a bit. I've got another delivery three days east, but I'm not in a rush.

Couriers don't stay anywhere long. Occupational hazard. But I'll be in the area if you need a resupply contact.

Find me at the marked waypoint on your map. I'll have water and basic provisions.

Don't get sentimental about it. It's business.

responses.text: [Sarcastic] 'Don't get sentimental.' You're a real charmer.

node_farewell_kind.text:
*almost smiles*

You're going to be fine.

Don't let the wasteland tell you otherwise.

Watch your six.

node_farewell_direct.text:
Good luck.

You'll need it — everyone does. But something tells me you'll make it.

Stay sharp.

node_farewell_sarcastic.text:
*actually laughs, brief*

Maybe. Survival does things to a person's social skills.

Get moving, wanderer. Clock's ticking.

quest_nodes.text:
Still working on it? You've got your inventory to check, your sidearm to equip, the radio to tune, and your map to open.

The wasteland doesn't pause for you. Get moving.

responses.next_inline: Inventory first. Then your sidearm. Radio. Map. In that order. Don't overthink it.

quest_nodes.text:
Look at that. You're actually ready.

Inventory checked. Sidearm equipped. Radio on. Map open. That's more than most people manage their first day out here.

Vault-Tec was right to send me after you. Don't make them regret it.

responses.text: [Friendly] Couldn't have done it without your help.
responses.next_inline: ...You could have. But I appreciate the sentiment. Take care of yourself.

responses.text: [Sarcastic] 'Don't make them regret it.' Classic Vault-Tec warmth.
responses.next_inline: *dry laugh* You're going to fit right in out here.
That's up to you now. The wasteland's big. Start exploring. The map will guide you.

emotional_nodes.text:
You're glowing, friend. Not metaphorically.

You've picked up significant radiation. Pop a RadAway before it gets worse. The effects sneak up on you — first your vision goes, then your judgment, then your grip on reality.

Treat it like a wound. Because it is one.

knowledge_nodes.text:
The gear? Standard Vault-Tec field issue.

Jumpsuit has radiation shielding woven into the lining. Won't stop a direct hit, but it buys time.

Sidearm is chambered for 9mm — clean, reliable, common ammo. You'll find rounds in almost any raider camp.

The stimpaks: inject into a major muscle group. The effect is fast but burns through quickly. Three shots won't get you through a firefight, so don't pick a fight you can't finish.

Bobby pins — don't lose them. Better than caps in some situations.

responses.text: [Sarcastic] You memorize gear specs for every delivery?
responses.next_inline: ...Yes. Clients who understand their equipment live longer. Couriers who deliver to surviving clients get paid. It's practical.

fallback.video_speech: Stay sharp, stay moving. The wasteland catches people off guard.
fallback.text: I don't have anything new for you right now. Stay sharp, stay moving. The wasteland has a way of catching people off guard.
